questions.question:
Which of the following pairs of 'soil - characteristics' is correct?

I. Sandy - proportion of fine particles is relatively higher

II. Clayey - greater proportion of big particles
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither I nor II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Soil

 
 
• Plants obtain inorganic elements from the soil, which serves as a natural medium for land plants. 
 
• Soil is the outer loose layer that covers the surface of Earth.
 
• Soil quality is a major determinant, along with climate, of plant distribution and growth.
 
• Soil quality depends not only on the chemical composition of the soil but also on the topography (regional surface features) and the presence of living organisms.
 
• In agriculture, the history of the soil, such as the cultivating practices and previous crops, modify the characteristics and fertility of that soil.
 
• Soil develops very slowly over long periods of time, and its formation results from natural and environmental forces acting on minerals, rock, and organic compounds.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sandy Soil

 
 
• Sandy Soil is light, warm, dry and tends to be acidic and low in nutrients.
 
• Sandy soils are often known as light soils due to their high proportion of sand and little clay.
 
• These soils have fast water drainage and are easy to work with.
 
• It mainly consists of rock particles such as limestone, shale, granite and quartz.
 
• Sandy Soil has a low percentage of organic material. Water travels through sandy soil very easily, so nutrients leach out quickly.
 
• Vegetable plants that thrive in sandy soil are Carrots, Radishes, Potatoes, Lettuce, Collard greens, Tomatoes, Zucchini, Corn, Asparagus, Watermelon, Beans, and Cucumber.
 
 

 
• Clay soil

 
 
• Clay soil is soil that is comprised of very fine mineral particles and not much organic material. 
 
• Clay is the smallest particle amongst the other two types of soil.
 
• The particles in this soil are tightly packed together with each other with very little or no airspace.
 
• This soil has very good water storage qualities and makes it hard for moisture and air to penetrate into it.
 
 
• It is very sticky to the touch when wet, but smooth when dried. 
 
 
 
• Clay is the densest and heaviest type of soil which that not drain well or provide space for plant roots to flourish.
 
• Clay can be used to make pots, pipes, and other useful objects that can be used for household purposes.
 
 
• Clay is used for manufacturing ceramic tiles as well that can be used for counters, floors, and walls.

• Ugadi, which is observed as Andhra Pradesh's Hindus' New Year's Day, is observed on the first day of the Hindu Luni-Solar Calendar in the month of Chaitra.

questions.question:
In which of the following ways, aggregate demand function is related to consumption function?

I. They have the same slope C.

II. The aggregate demand function is parallel to the consumption function.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The slope of the consumption function represents the marginal propensity to consume (MPC), which is the change in consumption resulting from a change in income.
 
• The aggregate demand function also includes consumption as a component, and therefore, the slope of the aggregate demand function is determined by the marginal propensity to consume. So, they have the same slope.
 
• The aggregate demand function consists of several components, including consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports.
 
• While the consumption function represents the relationship between consumption and income, the aggregate demand function represents the relationship between aggregate demand (total spending) and the overall price level.
 
• The aggregate demand function can be considered as the sum of all spending components, including consumption. Since consumption is a part of aggregate demand, the aggregate demand function and the consumption function are parallel to each other.

Therefore, both statements I and II are correct.

questions.question: Who is famously known as the Tiger of Mysore?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Tipu Sultan__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Tiger of Mysore

 
 
• Born in November 1750, Tipu Sultan was Haidar Ali’s son and a great warrior, also known as the Tiger of Mysore. Hence, Option 1 is correct.
 
• He was a well-educated man fluent in Arabic, Persian, Kanarese, and Urdu.
 
• Mysore had grown in strength under the leadership of powerful rulers like Haidar Ali (ruled from 1761 to 1782) and his famous son Tipu Sultan (ruled from 1782 to 1799).
 
• Tipu introduced several administrative innovations during his rule, including his coinage, a new Mauludi lunisolar calendar, and a new land revenue system which initiated the growth of the Mysore silk industry.
 
• Embracing Western military methods like artillery and rockets alongside traditional Indian weapons including war elephants, he ensured his forces could overwhelm his Indian rivals and match the British armies sent against him.
 
• He was also a patron of science and technology and is credited as the ‘pioneer of rocket technology in India.
 
• He wrote a military manual (Fathul Mujahidin) explaining the operation of rockets.
 
• Tipu was a great lover of democracy and a great diplomat who gave his support to the French soldiers at Seringapatam in setting up a Jacobin Club in 1797.
 
• Tipu himself became a member of the Jacobin Club and allowed himself to be called Citizen Tipu.
 
• He planted the Tree of Liberty at Seringapatam.

questions.question: What is the full form of HTTP?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Hypertext Transfer Protocol__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• HTTP stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol. Hypertext Transfer Protocol is an application protocol used for data communication. It is the base of data communication in the World Wide Web. It provides a standard for web browsers that facilitates users to exchange information over the internet.
 
• HTTP is used by most websites to access any file or page. HTTP is a request-response protocol in the client-server computing model. It is an application layer protocol designed within the framework of the Internet Protocol Suite.
 
• Hypertext - A text containing a link within it, is known as hypertext. If you click on a word on a webpage and it redirects you to a new page, it means you have clicked on a hypertext.​
 
• It is the protocol where encrypted HTTP data is transferred over a secure connection. It ensures data security over the network - mainly public networks like Wi-Fi.
 
• By virtue, HTTPS encryption is done bi-directionally, which means that the data is encrypted at both the client and server sides. Only the client can decode the information that comes from the server. So, HTTPS does the encryption of data between a client and a server, which protects against eavesdropping, forging of information, and tampering of data.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• HTTPS is HTTP with encryption.
 
• The only difference between the two protocols is that HTTPS uses TLS (SSL) to encrypt normal HTTP requests and responses. As a result, HTTPS is far more secure than HTTP.
 
• A website that uses HTTP has http:// in its URL, while a website that uses HTTPS has https://.

II. It was signed between the moderate and radical factions of Congress.

• This was the first time both the INC and the Muslim League's leaders had met in a joint session.
 
• The pact provided a joint political platform for the Moderates, Extremists, and the Muslim League. Hence statement II is correct.​

• Lucknow Pact was adopted by Congress at its Lucknow session on 29 December 1916.
 
• Lucknow Pact was adopted by the Muslim League on 31 December 1916.
 
• The Pact addressed both the structure of India's government and the relationship between Hindu and Muslim communities.
 
• This Lucknow pact prepared the door for Hindu-Muslim cooperation in the Khilafat movement, as well as Mohandas Gandhi's non-cooperation movement, which began in 1920.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Deccan Plateau is NOT correct?

options.text: The Deccan Plateau is higher in the west and slopes gently eastwards.
The Deccan Plateau is a triangular landmass.
An extension of the Plateau is also visible in the northeast.
The Satpura range flanks its broad base in the west.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'The Satpura range flanks its broad base in the west'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Deccan Plateau:**

 
 
• The Deccan Plateau is a large plateau located in southern India, characterized by its high altitude and rich volcanic soil, which supports diverse flora and fauna.
 
• This plateau is primarily a segment of the ancient Gondwanaland and includes parts of eight Indian states, stretching from the Satpura Range in the north to the Southern Indian ranges of the Eastern and Western Ghats.
 
• The plateau covers approximately 500,000 square kilometers, making it one of the largest plateaus in the world.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Features:**
 
 
• The Deccan Plateau is higher in the west and slopes gently eastwards, a characteristic that influences the flow of many rivers originating in the west and draining eastwards into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• This eastward slope is due to tectonic activity and the ancient geological processes that have shaped the land over millions of years.
 
• It forms a roughly triangular landmass, bounded by the Satpura and Vindhya Ranges to the north, the Eastern Ghats to the east, and the Western Ghats to the west.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Extension to the Northeast:**

 
 
• An extension of the Deccan Plateau is also visible in the northeast, where it merges into the Chota Nagpur Plateau. This area, rich in minerals, is crucial for India's mining industry.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Statement about the Satpura Range:**
 
 
• The Satpura range does not flank the Deccan Plateau’s broad base in the west. Instead, it is situated to the north of the plateau and runs parallel to the Vindhya Range. Together, they demarcate the boundary between the Indo-Gangetic plains and the Deccan Plateau.
 
• The Western Ghats, a continuous range running parallel to the western coast of India, is the range that borders the Deccan Plateau on the west.
 
 
 
• **Western and Eastern Ghats:**
 
 
• The Western Ghats are known for their biodiversity and are a UNESCO World Heritage site. They rise steeply from the west coast and descend gently towards the plateau.
 
• The Eastern Ghats are a series of discontinuous hills and mountains that run along India's eastern coast. These ranges are lower in elevation compared to the Western Ghats and are less continuous.

I. Lovlina Borgohain - Boxing

• She has won numerous medals for her country in the field of boxing, which confirms the first part of the statement as true.
 
 
 
• **Nikhat Zareen**, on the other hand, is also an** Indian sportsperson, but she is not a wrestler**.
 
 
• **She, too, is involved in boxing, not wrestling.**
 
• She is a former Junior World Champion and has represented India in various boxing championships.
 
 
 
• The misconception might arise due to the fact that both** Lovlina Borgohain and Nikhat Zareen are involved in combat sports.**
 
• However, they are both boxers and not involved in wrestling.
 
• Hence, statement II**, "Nikhat Zareen - Wrestling", is not correct while statement I, "Lovlina Borgohain - Boxing", is correct.**
 
• **Thus, the correct answer is 4) Only I.**

questions.question: Which country's moon mission has mapped out the global distribution of sodium on the Moon's surface in October 2022?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The X-ray spectrometer 'CLASS' on the Chandrayaan-2 Orbiter has mapped an abundance of sodium on the moon for the first time, according to ISRO.
 
• The findings of the spectrometer were published in 'The Astrophysical Journal Letters' in the last week of Sept 2022.
 
• The new findings will be helpful in the study of surface-exosphere interaction on the moon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chandrayaan-2 is India’s 2nd moon mission which was successfully launched by GSLV-MkIII-M1 from Second Launch Pad at Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• In 2019, Chandrayaan-2 was launched with an orbiter and a lander named Vikram, and a six-wheeled rover named Pragyaan ISRO.

questions.question: In which part of the Indian constitution are the provisions related to panchayat mentioned?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part IX**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Panchayati Raj

 
 
• Panchayati Raj is the system of local self-government of villages in rural India as opposed to urban and suburban municipalities.
 
• It consists of the Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) through which the self-government of villages is realized.
 
• They are tasked with "economic development, strengthening social justice and implementation of Central and State Government Schemes including those 29 subjects listed in the Eleventh Schedule."
 
• ​Part IX of the Indian Constitution is the section of the Constitution relating to the Panchayats.
 
• It stipulates that in states or Union Territories with more than two million inhabitants there are three levels of PRIs:
 
 
• Zilla Parishad at the District Level
 
• Panchayat Samiti at the Block Level
 
• Gram/Village Panchayat at the Village Level
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act,1992 added Article 243 to Article 243O and a new part Part IX to the constitution of India.
 
• Salient features of this Act:
 
 
• Gram Sabha (Article 243A):
 
 
• ​A body of all persons registered in the electoral roll of that Panchayat.
 
 
 
• Three-Tier System (Article 243B):
 
 
• ​Panchayat at the village, intermediate, and district levels.
 
 
 
• The election of members and chairpersons are given under Article 243B.
 
• Reservation of seats for SC/ST is provided at all three levels under Article 243D.
 
• The duration of Panchayats is given under Article 243E, it is constituted for five years.
 
• Grounds of disqualification are given under Article 243F.
 
• Powers, authorities, and responsibilities are given in Article 243G and enlisted in the 11th schedule of the constitution.
 
• State Election Commission (243K) for superintendence, control, and direction of the election in Panchayats.

questions.question: The Young Bengal Movement was founded by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Henry Louis Vivian Derozio__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Henry Louis Vivian Derozio__ is the founder of the Young Bengal movement.
 
• Henry Louis Vivian Derozio: 
 __
 
• He was an Indian poet of Portuguese origin and assistant headmaster of Hindu College, Kolkata.
 
• He was a radical thinker of his time and one of the first Indian educators to disseminate Western learning and science among the young men of Bengal.
 
• He joined the Hindu College as a teacher at the age of seventeen.
 
• He and his students called DErozians or Young Bengal promoted radical reformist ideas among the people of Bengal. 
 
• He was a poet, novelist, and writer. He was also the first nationalist poet of modern India.
 
• The " Fakeer of Jungheera" is a long poem by Henry Louis Vivian Derozio.
 
• Most of the work in found to Indian religion, culture, rule and regulation, rigidity, culture, etc.
 
• Derozio died of cholera at an early age of 22 on 26 December 1831 in Calcutta. His body was buried in the South Park Street Cemetery of Kolkata.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Dayananda Saraswati

 
 
• Dayananda Saraswati [1824-1883] was the first to give the call for Swarajya – "India for Indians" – in 1876.
 
• For his own inspiration, Swami Dayanand went to the Vedas which he regarded as infallible.
 
• He rejected all later religious thought if it conflicted with the Vedas.
 
• This total dependence on Vedas and their infallibility gave his teachings orthodox coloring.
 
• He was opposed to idolatry, ritual, and priesthood and particularly to the prevalent caste practices and popular Hinduism as preached by brahmins.
 
• ​Swami Dayanand met Keshub Chandra Sen, Vidyasagar, Justice Ranade, Gopal Hari Deshmukh, and other modern religious and social reformers.
 
• He took inspiration from the Vedas and considered them to be ‘India’s Rock of Ages, the infallible, and the true original seed of Hinduism. 
 
• He gave the slogan “Back to the Vedas”.
 
• Dayananda’s slogan of ‘Back to the Vedas’ was a call for a revival of Vedic learning and Vedic purity of religion and not a revival of Vedic times.
 
• He accepted modernity and displayed a patriotic attitude to national problems.
 
 
 
• Lala Hansraj
 
 
• ​Anglo-Vedic colleges or schools are also known as Dayanand Anglo-Vedic schools.
 
• Dayanand Anglo Vedic (DAV) Schools were founded in 1886 in Lahore by the efforts of Mahatma Hansraj in memory of Swami Dayanand Saraswati.
 
• The schools were run by the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic College Trust & Management Society, also known as the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic Education Society.
 
• DAV institutions are the best place to study and work together.
 
• Under the DAV family, there are 900 schools, 75 colleges, and a university.
 
• “DAV Movement” founded in 1886 by Lala Lajpat Rai (Father of the DAV Movement) picked up momentum due to the arduous efforts of Lala Lajpat Rai, Mahatma Hans Raj, Pandit Gurudutt Vidyarthi, and many others dedicated as the Arya Samaj activist. 
 
 
 
• Keshub Chandra Sen (also spelled Keshab Chunder Sen) was born in an affluent family of Calcutta on 19 November 1838.
 
 
• In 1857, he joined the Brahmo Samaj and took up studying philosophy.
 
• Sen was inspired by Christian teachings and sought to fuse Christian teachings into the Hindu framework.
 
• He thought that only the Christian doctrine would help instill new life into Hindu society.
 
• He was also impressed with the discipline of Christian missionary work and started following it himself.
 
• His lean towards Christianity caused a rift between him and Tagore and he broke away from the Samaj and formed the Bharat Barshiya Brahmo Samaj (Brahmo Samaj of India).

questions.question: According to which of the following laws, the pressure of a mixture of gases is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of the component gases?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dalton's Law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dalton's Law:**

 
 
• **Definition: **Dalton's Law, also known as the Law of Partial Pressures, states that **the total pressure exerted by a mixture of gases is the sum of the partial pressures of the individual gases.**
 
• **Partial Pressure: **The pressure that each gas would exert if it alone occupied the entire volume of the mixture is its partial pressure.
 
• **Independent Behaviour: **The law assumes that gases behave independently of each other, meaning the pressure of each gas in a mixture is unaffected by the presence of other gases.
 
• **Applications: **Dalton's Law has important applications in many areas including chemistry, physics, physiology, and even scuba diving, where understanding the pressures of different gas components is crucial.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Law
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Charles' Law
 States that the volume of a given mass of an ideal gas is directly proportional to the absolute temperature provided its pressure remains constant.
 
 

 Boyle's Law
 Proposes an inverse relationship between the pressure and volume of a gas, assuming the temperature is kept constant within a closed system.
 
 

 Graham's Law
 
 
Describes the relationship between the rates of diffusion of gases and their molar masses.

 
It states that the rate of diffusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its molar mass.

__
 
• El Nino is a surroundings layout that depicts the odd warming of surface waters in the Japanese tropical Pacific Ocean.
 
• El Nino is a weather circumstance that happens in the Pacific Ocean.
 
• The term** El Niño (**Spanish for 'the **Christ Child**') refers to a warming of the ocean surface, or above-average sea surface temperatures, in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean.
 
• The low-level surface winds, which normally blow from **east to west** along the equator (**“easterly winds**”), instead weaken or, in some cases, start blowing the other direction (from west to east or “westerly winds”).
 
• El Niño recurs irregularly, from two years to a decade, and no two events are exactly alike. El Niño events can disrupt normal weather patterns in the United States and globally.
 
• Los Angeles Nina is a surroundings layout that depicts the cooling of floor sea waters along the tropical west shore of South the united states.

 Gulf Stream
 
 
 
• The Gulf Stream is a strong ocean current that brings warm water from the Gulf of Mexico into the Atlantic Ocean.
 
• It extends all the way up the eastern coast of the United States and Canada.
 
• The Gulf Stream is caused by a large system of circular currents and powerful winds, called an oceanic gyre.
 
 
 
 

 West Wind
 
 
 
• A current in the southern hemisphere moving from west to east at approximately 40°-55°S, caused by prevailing western cold winds.
 
• It encircles the earth, crossing the Atlantic, Indian, and Pacific oceans
 
 
 
 

 Peru Current
